about: Local state scenarios on a real filesystem (appendix A 27-29, and the plan's protection and tab contracts that replace the old ones). Each scenario states the starting files, the action, and what must hold afterwards. Contexts are the query identity a file or handle is bound to (command, target, sort or tab, filters, normalized window, the Threads account). All state lives under the skill's data/ directory (THREADS_DATA_DIR in tests).

collection.fact: --out writes NDJSON: a header line (query context, format version, started_at), then records, each page closed by a kind:page marker (cursor, ids, n, stop_reason). Only complete pages are trusted: on resume the tail after the last marker is dropped and re-read. A file for another query, an older format or the previous skill's format is refused before any byte changes. A marker whose ids or n disagree with the records above it is an integrity failure. The file is opened without following a symlink, mode 0600, locked without waiting; writes are fsynced. A file whose last marker says the surface ended (exhausted or window_reached) is complete and requests nothing.

handles.fact: A handle is a monotonically increasing number bound to its query context and the Threads account. The counter reservation is fsynced before the handle file is written, so a crash leaves a gap, never a reused number; the counter is never deleted or lowered. Handles expire after a TTL and are cleaned up by the skill itself (the model is never told to delete them). Files are 0600 in a 0700 directory.

protection.fact: Account protection state is written atomically (temporary file, fsync, replace). State that cannot be read counts as blocked (fail closed). A checkpoint blocks until a person clears it; a rate limit blocks for 30 minutes and never downgrades an existing checkpoint. Requests are spaced 1-2 seconds apart at random; the next allowed time is recorded before a request starts. Check, budget, pacing, the request, its classification and a new block happen under one cross-process lock. Every charged request is appended to an observation log (time, kind) kept for 24 hours; the log is never enforced.

tab_protection.fact: The dedicated tab classifies the app's own responses too (a hook installed once per page load reads GraphQL and route bodies and document moves to /challenge, /checkpoint or /accounts/login) and writes what it saw, with the time, to that tab's sessionStorage, which survives a reload of the same tab but not a lost tab. Every call reads that record, the tab's location and the tab ledger's 429s before sending anything, moves a seen signal into data/protection as a block, and only then clears the tab's record. A call that records a block blanks the dedicated tab to about:blank (no request) so the app's background polling stops. A newly opened tab is checked (location, statuses seen while loading, the document's checkpoint and login markers) before any query. The sessionStorage path depends on P2 R1(b); if it does not hold, this contract is undecided and goes to the P2 gate.
tab_protection.verify: P2 R1 (a) when the hook is installed, (b) sessionStorage survives a reload in an Aside tab, (c) whether the app moves itself to /challenge on a checkpoint

session.fact: One dedicated Threads tab per Aside account, recorded by targetId in data/session/<account>.json. Find, re-check, open and record happen under one session lock, so concurrent starts open one tab. Only a targetId the skill recorded is its tab; a tab found by URL is never adopted. A corrupt session file reopens a tab once and says so.
